title: Space hierarchy theorem
statement: Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be space-constructible functions. Suppose that for every $A\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $N$ such that $A f(n)\le g(n)$ for every $n\ge N$. Then $\mathrm{SPACE}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{SPACE}(g)$, where each class consists of languages decidable by a finite binary Turing machine using at most a constant multiple of the indicated space bound.
hypotheses_covered: f and g are functions from natural numbers to natural numbers
For every natural number A there exists N such that for every n ≥ N, A · f(n) ≤ g(n)
